## Summary

This study used bulk RNA-seq of iPSC-derived (i3) cortical neurons with TDP-43 loss to characterize cryptic alternative polyadenylation (APA) events, comparing TDP-43-depleted cells against controls. The authors developed a bioinformatic pipeline to detect alternative last exons, 3'UTR extensions, and intronic polyadenylation, finding that TDP-43 binding sites are enriched at these cryptic APA loci and that TDP-43 can both repress and enhance such events. These cryptic APA categories were also validated in postmortem ALS and FTD brain tissue, and complementary SLAM-seq and ribosome profiling data showed that different cryptic APA types have distinct effects on transcript stability and translation. This dataset serves as a key TDP-43 knockdown comparator for cryptic-polyadenylation analyses in ALS/FTD.

series_summaries.title: TDP-43 loss induces cryptic polyadenylation in ALS/FTD [humphrey-i3-cortical]
series_summaries.summary: Nuclear depletion and cytoplasmic aggregation of the RNA-binding protein TDP-43 is the hallmark of ALS, occurring in over 97% of cases. A key consequence of TDP-43 nuclear loss is the de-repression of cryptic exons. Whilst TDP-43 regulated cryptic splicing is increasingly well catalogued, cryptic alternative polyadenylation (APA) events, which define the 3’ end of last exons, have been largely overlooked, especially when not associated with novel upstream splice junctions. We developed a bioinformatic pipeline to reliably identify distinct APA event types: alternative last exons (ALE), 3’UTR extensions (3’Ext) and ‘ composite ’ intronic polyadenylation (IPA) events. We identified novel neuronal cryptic APA sites induced by TDP-43 loss of function by systematically applying our pipeline to a compendium of publicly available and in house datasets. We find that TDP-43 binding sites and target motifs are enriched at these cryptic events and that TDP-43 can have both repressive and enhancing action on APA. Importantly, all categories of cryptic APA can also be identified in ALS and FTD post mortem brain regions with TDP-43 proteinopathy underlining their potential disease relevance. RNA-seq and Ribo-seq analyses indicate that distinct cryptic APA categories have different downstream effects on transcript and translation. Intriguingly, cryptic 3’Exts occur in multiple transcription factors, such as ELK1 , SIX3, and TLX1, and lead to an increase in RNA stability. 3’Exts are localised to the cytoplasm and neurites and translated leading to an increase in wild-type protein levels. In summary, we demonstrate that TDP-43 nuclear depletion induces a novel category of cryptic RNA processing events and we expand the palette of TDP-43 loss consequences by showing this can also lead to an increase in normal protein translation.
series_summaries.overall_design: short-read bulk RNA-sequencing of day 30 IPSC-derived cortical neurons with and without TDP-43 knockdown (6 controls, 6 TDP-43 knockdowns)

studies.summary: This study combined single-nucleus RNA sequencing of postmortem ALS spinal cords, single-cell profiling of SOD1G93A ALS mouse spinal cords, and human iPSC-derived motor neuron/astrocyte/microglia tri-cultures to characterize glial state changes in ALS. Comparison of ALS versus control spinal cord tissue revealed glial populations with increased inflammatory and activation marker expression, with many signals converging on receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) and the necroptosis pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity in SOD1G93A mice delayed symptom onset and motor impairment and altered glial responses, while iPSC tri-cultures were used to identify secreted biomarkers of RIPK1 activation that were also modulated by RIPK1 inhibition in CSF from ALS patients. Together, the findings implicate inflammatory RIPK1 signaling and ALS-enriched glial states as contributors to disease pathogenesis.

studies.readme_body:
## Summary

This study combined single-nucleus RNA sequencing of postmortem ALS spinal cords, single-cell profiling of SOD1G93A ALS mouse spinal cords, and human iPSC-derived motor neuron/astrocyte/microglia tri-cultures to characterize glial state changes in ALS. Comparison of ALS versus control spinal cord tissue revealed glial populations with increased inflammatory and activation marker expression, with many signals converging on receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) and the necroptosis pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity in SOD1G93A mice delayed symptom onset and motor impairment and altered glial responses, while iPSC tri-cultures were used to identify secreted biomarkers of RIPK1 activation that were also modulated by RIPK1 inhibition in CSF from ALS patients. Together, the findings implicate inflammatory RIPK1 signaling and ALS-enriched glial states as contributors to disease pathogenesis.

## Notes

GSE287256 is bulk RNA-seq companion, not single-cell.

## Samples

n_samples_or_datasets: 46

series_summaries.title: Single cell RNAseq of iPSC tri-cultures treated with necroptosis inducer
series_summaries.summary: Transcriptomic analysis of iPSC tri-culture (microglia, neurons, astrocytes) stimulated with Tnf, Smac, and Zvad (TSZ) to trigger necroptosis pathway activation, in the presence or absence of a Ripk1 inhibitor
series_summaries.overall_design: Cells were pre-treated for 1 hour with 1 μM Smac mimetic LCL161 (Selleck Chem, S7009), 20 μM zVAD-fmk (Enzo Life Sciences, ALX-260-020), and 1 μM RIPK1 inhibitor GSK’547 prior to a 4 hour incubation with 50 ng/mL recombinant human TNF (R&D Systems, 210-TA). Four hours after treatment, cells were collected and sequenced using the 10x Genomics platform.

series_summaries.title: Spinal cord single-nuclei RNA sequencing of human ALS spinal cords [ALS human snRNAseq]
series_summaries.summary: Transcriptomic analysis of postmortem cervical spinal cord samples from 8 people with ALS (6 sporadic and 2 familial cases) and 4 age-matched non-neurological controls using snRNA-seq
series_summaries.overall_design: Spinal cords were acquired from the NIH brain biobank, nuclei were isolated by FACS, and sequenced using 10x Genomics and Illumina platforms.

series_summaries.title: Bulk RNA sequencing of human ALS spinal cords
series_summaries.summary: There remains a poor understanding of cell-specific responses in the human ALS spinal cord, including differences in cell type composition, changes in cell state, and contribution of various cell types to neuroinflammation.
series_summaries.overall_design: Transcriptomic analysis of postmortem cervical spinal cord samples from 8 people with ALS (6 sporadic and 2 familial cases) and 4 age-matched non-neurological controls

series_summaries.title: Single cell RNAseq of SOD1 mouse spinal cords
series_summaries.summary: Sequencing was performed to better understand the role of neuroinflammation and glial RIPK1 signaling in ALS pathogenesis in the SOD1G93A transgenic mouse model.
series_summaries.overall_design: Starting on postnatal day 70, before noticeable motor deficits, female mice were treated prophylactically with the tool compound GSK’547 (RIPK1i), a highly selective CNS-penetrant RIPK1 kinase inhibitor. The inhibitor was initially dosed in chow and as motor symptoms became more severe, RIPK1i was administered via oral gavage. Spinal cords were removed at day 120 for analysis.
